content: The Open Source Center (OSC) is a United States government agency that provides analysts with access to open-source materials, including gray literature, through its domestic and overseas bureaus. It was established on November 1, 2005, under the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) with the goal of enhancing the availability of open-source information for intelligence officers and other government officials. The OSC supplies materials to the National Technical Information Service (NTIS) and other government officials via an online news service called World News Connection. Within the Intelligence Community, the OSC plays a critical role in ensuring access to open-source intelligence. In the legislative process, Congressman McCurdy served as the counterpart on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. The House version of the legislation included a proposal for a separate Open Source Office, an idea suggested by Larry Prior, a Marine Reservist with experience in the Marine Corps Intelligence Center (MCIC) and a staff member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. In 1996, the Aspin-Brown Commission reported that U.S. access to open-source materials was severely deficient and recommended that addressing this issue should be a top priority for both funding and the attention of the Director of Central Intelligence (DCI). Later, in its July 2004 report, the 9/11 Commission recommended the creation of an open-source intelligence agency, though it did not provide further details or commentary. Subsequently, the WMD Commission (also known as the Robb-Silberman Commission) issued a report in March 2005 recommending the establishment of an Open Source Directorate within the CIA. Following these recommendations, in November 2005, the Director of National Intelligence announced the creation of the DNI Open Source Center. The OSC was established to collect information from a wide range of sources, including the Internet, databases, press, radio, television, video, geospatial data, photographs, and commercial imagery. Beyond collecting openly available information, the OSC also trains analysts to make more effective use of this data. The Center absorbed the CIA's pre-existing Foreign Broadcast Information Service (FBIS), which had been originally established in 1941. Douglas Naquin, the head of FBIS, was appointed as the director of the newly formed Open Source Center.
